clue.text: See Holstein's fantastic footballers!

indicators.note: something fantastic is fanciful and unreal, so the letters before it are reshaped freely

parts.note: all twelve letters, the possessive S included

explanation.surface: An invitation to watch a club's (or Holstein Kiel's) star players perform brilliantly.
explanation.walkthrough: THE LIONESSES is the nickname of the England women's football team.
explanation.definitionFit: The England women's national team are known by this nickname, so the players are a group of footballers.

clue.text: Most High to examine everyone within

indicators.note: within says one word is placed inside the other, the examining word wrapping the everyone word

parts.note: to test is to examine
everyone means all

explanation.surface: A religious phrase: God, the Most High, is to examine all of us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most High' reads as a title for God, but here it is just a superlative.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of high or tall describes whatever reaches the greatest height.

clue.text: Eastern sea creature shedding tail in spring

indicators.note: shedding a tail means losing the final letter of the creature's name

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for eastern
the manatee is a large aquatic mammal, the sea cow

explanation.surface: An oriental marine animal moults its tail in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season but is a verb: to issue or arise from a source.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to flow out or originate from a source, as to spring from it does.

clue.text: Similar in every detail, papers a client misplaced

parts.note: ID means identity papers

indicators.note: misplaced letters are put in the wrong positions, so they must be rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A lawyer's lost documents for a client turn up, matching the originals exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are exactly alike are the same in every respect, matching detail for detail.

clue.text: One billion stolen from dope? Impressive!

indicators.note: something stolen from a word is taken out of it, leaving the rest behind

parts.note: to nobble a racehorse is to dope it
B is the abbreviation for billion

explanation.surface: A billion-pound drugs haul has been taken, and the reaction is admiration.
explanation.walkthrough: To nobble is British slang for drugging a racehorse to stop it winning; one of its two Bs goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Noble describes something grand and stately in appearance, which is what impressive means.

clue.text: Drunk amid mounting litter? Divorce results!

indicators.note: amid puts the drunk word in the middle of the litter word
in a down entry, mounting means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a litter is a set of young, such as puppies
lit is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A drunken partner among an ever-growing pile of rubbish leads to the end of a marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Litter' suggests rubbish, but it is a brood of young animals.
explanation.definitionFit: To split up is to separate as a couple, the informal equivalent of divorcing.

clue.text: Composer wanting area green for painter

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the composer's name is missing the area letter

parts.note: Edward Elgar, English composer
A is the abbreviation for area
eco- means environmentally friendly, green

explanation.surface: A musician lacking open space, perhaps a park, swaps careers to become an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: El Greco was the Cretan-born painter of Renaissance Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: El Greco was a celebrated sixteenth-century artist, so he is an example of a painter.

clue.text: Leicester won somehow without a song sung for 1 Across?

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the jumbled letters sit around the single letter
somehow says the letters come together in some unstated arrangement

parts.note: the letters of these two words
taken as written

explanation.surface: Leicester somehow won, yet no song was sung in honour of the England women's team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like lacking, but means outside. Sweet Caroline, the Neil Diamond song, became the Lionesses' anthem during their Euro 2022 win.
explanation.definitionFit: England fans adopted this Neil Diamond hit as a terrace chant for the women's team, so it is sung for them.

clue.text: Corrected draft seen in no great poem

indicators.note: a corrected text has been altered and reordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these four words

explanation.surface: An editor's verdict: once fixed, the draft shows no sign of being a great poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word but is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inferno, first part of Dante's Divine Comedy, is one of the masterpieces of Italian verse.

clue.text: Defensive structure great for Scottish hero

parts.note: a wall is built for defence
ace means excellent, great

explanation.surface: A sturdy rampart proved a boon to a celebrated Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: William Wallace led Scottish resistance against English rule in the thirteenth century, a national champion.

clue.text: An attempt by Chuck to return sausage

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the assembled letters are read from the end

parts.note: taken as written
a go is an attempt
to lob is to throw, chuck

explanation.surface: Someone named Chuck tries to send back a sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chuck' poses as a man's name but is a verb, to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Bologna is a large smoked sausage named after the Italian city, the original of baloney.

clue.text: Stylish English worker entertaining cricket side

indicators.note: to entertain is to host or take in, so the outer letters hold the cricket word

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a worker ant
the leg side is one half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A fashionable English employee hosts a cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field divides into the off side and the leg side, so 'side' is not a team.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone graceful and fashionable in dress or manner.

clue.text: Petition beginning to exercise new doctor

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter
N is the abbreviation for new
to doctor a patient is to treat them

explanation.surface: A newly qualified physician is asked to start a patient on an exercise programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a noun but is the verb to treat.
explanation.definitionFit: Petition as a verb means to ask earnestly, which is to entreat or beg.

clue.text: Smart female copper with Bond

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a tie is a bond

explanation.surface: A clever policewoman teams up with James Bond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a police officer and 'Bond' the spy; both are ordinary words here. Smart means good-looking, as in a smart outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutie is an attractive, appealing woman, and smart here carries its sense of looking neat and attractive.

clue.text: Supporters of team such as 1 Across?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: people who stand up for a cause
second meaning: winners of a title, as the England women were in Euro 2022

explanation.surface: Fans of a side like England's women.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one phrase about fans; it is two meanings, joined by 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A champion is an advocate for a cause and also the winner of a competition, which the England women's team became.

clue.text: Almost lost Asian ruler in Russian city

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: astray means lost
a khan is a ruler in central Asia

explanation.surface: An Asian monarch is nearly lost somewhere in Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrakhan is a port on the Volga delta in southern Russia, giving its name to curly lambskin.

clue.text: Swimmer embarrassed by hilarious hairstyle

parts.note: red in the face, embarrassed
the mullet, short at the front and long at the back, often mocked

explanation.surface: A swimmer is mortified by a laughable haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' suggests a person, but is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Red mullet is a sea fish, and in crosswords a swimmer is often any fish.

clue.text: Taj Mahal location in dull illustration

indicators.note: in places the location's name inside the word for dull

parts.note: dim means dull
the Taj Mahal stands in Agra, India

explanation.surface: A boring picture of where the Taj Mahal stands.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagram is a simple drawing that explains something, a kind of illustration.

clue.text: Outstrip London-bound coach?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to outshine or steal attention from
second meaning, playful: a stagecoach going up, as journeys to the capital are said to go up

explanation.walkthrough: In British usage you travel up to London from anywhere, and a stage is a stagecoach; the question mark flags the split reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To upstage someone is to draw attention away from them, outdoing them in the spotlight.

clue.text: 1 Across opponents s-suffering?

parts.note: the stammered letter, taken as written
pain is suffering

explanation.surface: A stammered cry of anguish from rivals of the England women.
explanation.walkthrough: Spain beat the Lionesses in the 2023 World Cup final, so their opponents are suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain's women's team faced England in the 2023 Women's World Cup final, making them the Lionesses' rivals.

clue.text: Small onion all you'll get, do we hear?

indicators.note: asking what we hear means the answer goes by its sound, not the spelling

parts.note: you'll is you shall, and lot means all you get, as in that's your lot

explanation.surface: A stingy cook warns that one little onion is your whole ration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's your lot' is British for 'that is all you get'; shall and lot, run together, give the vegetable's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallot is a small, mild member of the onion family that grows in clusters.

clue.text: Score-settler against foe at last in fury

indicators.note: in puts these letters inside the word for fury

parts.note: fury is great anger
V is short for versus, against

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the enemy word

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: Someone takes on an enemy in a final rage to settle the score.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenger takes revenge for a wrong, settling an old score with the culprit.

clue.text: Affair in which adult is eaten by one chasing 1 Across?

indicators.note: something eaten is swallowed inside, so the adult letters go inside the predator word

parts.note: a lion pursues lionesses as mates
A is the film certificate for adult
taken as written

explanation.surface: A romance in which a grown-up is devoured by a big cat pursuing females.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'is' of 'is eaten' does double duty: it joins the inserted letters as well as reading as the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a secret romantic or sexual relationship, an affair.

clue.text: Can't do without Geordies called Edward?

indicators.note: how Geordies call a name is how it sounds in their Tyneside accent

parts.note: Ned is the pet name for Edward, and several of them are Neds

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about why so many Newcastle men are named Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: Geordies are people from Newcastle upon Tyne; in their accent the short vowel of Neds is said nearer to needs.
explanation.definitionFit: To need something is to be unable to do without it, so the verb forms match.

clue.text: Answer arrived about Donne's case in scholarly life

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for answer

indicators.note: about means around, so the arrived word wraps the poet's letters

parts.note: came means arrived

indicators.note: a case is the outside, so only the first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the outside letters of the poet's name

explanation.surface: A reply concerning John Donne's predicament in academia has turned up.
explanation.definitionFit: Academe is the world of universities and learning, the scholarly life lived there.

clue.text: European sailor hurried round to tell story

indicators.note: turned round means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European
tar is an old word for sailor
ran means hurried

explanation.surface: A continental seaman rushed around to spin a yarn.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate is to give an account of events, telling a story aloud or in writing.

clue.text: Virtue-signaller seen with low-down element

parts.note: a halo marks out a saint's goodness in paintings
gen is British slang for information, the low-down

explanation.surface: A sanctimonious person caught with sordid information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Virtue-signaller' suggests a sanctimonious person but is the halo, which literally signals virtue.
explanation.definitionFit: The halogens, such as chlorine and iodine, are a group of chemical elements, so one is an element.

clue.text: Roman emperor keeping young male ape

indicators.note: keeping means holding on to, so the emperor title holds the young male inside

parts.note: imperator, the Latin title of a Roman commander and emperor
a son is a young male relative

explanation.surface: A Caesar keeps a pet primate as a juvenile male.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ape' looks like a primate noun but means a mimic, one who apes others.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape is to mimic, so an ape in the noun sense of copier is an impersonator.
